questions.question: What must a JSX expression return?
options: Multiple sibling elements with no wrapper
A single root element or fragment
questions.explanation: JSX must have one enclosing root element, or you can use a fragment (<>...</>) to avoid adding an extra DOM node.

questions.question: Which attribute name is correct in JSX for a click handler?
questions.explanation: JSX attributes use camelCase, so DOM event handlers are named like onClick, onChange, etc.

questions.question: Why should you avoid mutating props inside a component?
options: Props are read-only by convention; mutating them breaks the one-way data flow from parent to child
JavaScript throws a runtime error when you mutate an object
It only matters for class components
It has no real effect either way
questions.explanation: Props flow one direction, parent to child. Treating them as immutable keeps data flow predictable and avoids subtle bugs when the parent re-renders.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the special `children` prop?
options: It lists a component's child components in an array for debugging
It lets a component render whatever nested content is passed between its opening and closing tags
It is only used internally by React DevTools
It replaces the need for props entirely
questions.explanation: `children` is how wrapper/layout components (like a Card) render arbitrary nested JSX passed to them by a parent.
